Subject: Post-call: BrightFin integration qualification & structured-output reliability

Hi Samir / Priya — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick written recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Call highlights
- Primary use case: customer support ticket summarization → embeddings for retrieval + a reranker to surface the top 3 candidate answers.
- Reliability ask: deterministic, schema-constrained outputs for the structured summary block (JSON) plus clear retry behavior when decoding fails.
- Nonfunctional: sub-150ms median latency for reranker at 256-token context + cost target we discussed on the call.

Technical notes (short)
- SDK/auth: we recommend using Redwood SDK with short-lived token auth (examples attached).
- Routing: pin to us-west region for low latency; we can configure routing rules for prod vs. dev.
- Structured output: provide JSON schema and use constrained decoding + validation on response; fallback policy to a lighter model variant on failure.

Attachments and artifacts
- redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (covers endpoints, auth, config knobs)
- schema-example.json (example of the constrained output we propose)

Proposed next steps
1) Share a short tech contact for your engineering lead (we’ll add them to a technical kickoff).
2) Redwood provides a 2-week POC plan (we’ll spin up a dedicated test pool + canary routing).
3) We’ll produce a short SOW draft and timeline (attached: sow-draft.pdf).

Can you confirm: 1) engineering contact, 2) target date to start POC (we can begin as early as 12/20), and 3) any procurement constraints we should be aware of?

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

—

Thanks Vanessa — good recap. A few clarifying questions from our side before we loop in engineering:

- Reranker latency: you mentioned sub-150ms median at 256 tokens. Is that for a single-item rerank or batched reranking? We typically send batches of 16 candidates.
- Failure modes: what exactly triggers the fallback to the lighter model? Is that based on schema validation failure, latency threshold, or token budget?
- POC duration: we prefer a two-week POC but need to understand what measurable signals you’ll provide to show reliability (SLOs / validation pass rate).

Procurement note: we’ll need the SOW and an initial license/commit estimate to circulate with Finance. Priya is on copy.

Great questions — answers below and a short POC acceptance criteria proposal.

Answers
- Reranker latency: the 150ms median figure was measured for batched reranking (batch size 16) on the dedicated pool we run for similar customers. We’ll include a latency breakdown in the POC dashboard (p50/p90/p99).
- Fallback triggers: primary trigger is schema validation failure (we run constrained decoding + a lightweight post-validate step). Secondary trigger is latency breach > 500ms for a request — in that case traffic is routed to a configured cheaper/fast variant.
- Signals: POC dashboard will include validation pass rate (per prompt template set), end-to-end latency distributions, and retrieval/embedding recall metrics.

POC proposal (2 weeks)
- Week 0 (prep): share engineering contact, configure dev pool, ingest a small sample (5k tickets) for embeddings.
- Week 1: run integration, enable constrained decoding + JSON schema validation; iterate on schema; collect metrics.
- Week 2: run load test with batch=16 reranking; evaluate pass rate and latency; produce a short findings doc.

Attached: updated schema-example.json and a draft SOW (sow-draft.pdf) with milestones and success criteria.

If this looks good I’ll schedule a 30m kickoff with your engineering lead + our solutions engineer (Karthik) early next week.

—
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: engineering checklist for BrightFin POC (SDK/auth/routing)

Vanessa / Aditya — quick internal tech checklist to attach to the kickoff. Share with Samir’s eng lead once they’re onboarded.

1) SDK & auth- Use Redwood SDK v2.3; recommend short-lived bearer tokens (we’ll provision test tokens scoped to the dev pool).- Example header: Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>

2) Routing / region pinning- Add header X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2 for deterministic routing to the dedicated pool.- For canary: X-Redwood-Canary: true on 5% of traffic.

3) Structured output validation- Constrained decoding config: enable model-level constraints + sampling top-p=0.0 for deterministic decoding when using strict schema.- Post-validate flow: retry up to 2 times with exponential backoff if the JSON fails validation. On repeated failure, trigger light-variant fallback.

4) Embeddings / reranker config- Use batch size 16 for rerank requests; measure model GPU_util and queue latency to tune.- Use prefix KV-caching for repeated contexts (ticket templates) to reduce token consumption.

5) Observability hooks- Expose validation_pass boolean and validation_error_codes in the response metadata so BrightFin can ingest into their monitoring.

Attachment: schema-example.json (will be shared in the kickoff).

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
